info.description:
**Unofficial software.** `franklinwh-modbus-bridge` is not endorsed, supported, or
affiliated with FranklinWH in any way. Provided **"AS IS"**, for educational
and informational purposes only, without warranty of any kind, express or
implied. The authors and contributors accept no responsibility or liability
for any consequences of its use.

This API issues **write commands to grid-connected battery hardware**. You
assume all risk, including risk to your hardware, your warranty and your
electricity supply.

**Compliance.** Keep your system compliant with the settings your official
FranklinWH app or installer configured — they may enforce battery and gateway
safety, your local grid profile and import/export limits, or incentive/VPP
programme conditions. Using this API to bypass them is entirely at your own
risk and is neither condoned nor encouraged.

**Do not contact FranklinWH support about this software.** Report bugs and
request features at [https://github.com/david2069/franklinwh-modbus-bridge/issues](https://github.com/david2069/franklinwh-modbus-bridge/issues).

Full terms: [LICENSE](https://github.com/david2069/franklinwh-modbus-bridge/blob/main/LICENSE) · SunSpec conformance:
[PICS SM-000028](https://sunspec.org/wp-content/uploads/2009/03/UPDATED_FranklinWH_Modbus_PICS_SM-000028.xlsx)

get.description:
Outage-aware connectivity: per-gateway connected/last-good-poll state plus
recent outages. Powers the scheduler's outage view (WiFi→4G drops etc.).

The bridge's background loops and when each last ran (#324 §11 C).

``{ok, counts, stale[], broken[], workers[]}``, the DC bridge's shape. A
stalled worker is reported here and as WORKER_STALLED; it never fails the
health check, so the platform doesn't restart away the evidence.

schema.title: Response Health Workers Api Health Workers Get

get.description:
The bridge's status. Answers with no gateway named: it is the add-on's
health check. The poller component lists every gateway; ``?gateway=``
(ID or serial) adds that gateway's poller as the flat fields (#296 item 43:
no silent fallback to the gateway with ID 'default').

post.description: Verify credentials, set the session cookie. Accepts form or JSON.

get.description:
Why a login ended. No auth: it's asked by a page that just got a 401.

``sid`` is the login id the page saved at login time; it is a random
secret only that browser holds. If the record says the login is still
open but the browser has stopped presenting it, it is ended here with the
reason that fits (idle past the cookie lifetime = expired, else the
browser dropped it), so the audit trail has it too.

schema.title: Response Session Status Api Auth Session Status Get

post.description: Change your own password. Your other logins end; this one stays.

schema.title: Response Me Api Auth Me Get

get.description: Logins, most recently active first. ``active=true`` = still open.

post.description: End one login now; its page shows "An administrator ended this login".

get.description:
Audit trail: logins, failed logins, logouts, logins ended (newest first).

``username`` (as typed at sign-in, any case) and ``event`` narrow it.
The address of one gateway (the primary one unless ``gateway_id``).
Test TCP connectivity to a gateway's configured host:port.

schema.title: Response Test Gateway Api Gateway Test Get

get.description: The SunSpec catalog captured for a gateway (the primary one unless named).

Flat list of catalog points with metadata + whether each is published
(promoted into an enabled group). Powers the Explorer → group picker.

Export a gateway's SunSpec models with their current values (#228).

``models``: comma-separated model ids; empty for every model.
``format``: ``json`` or ``csv``. ``redact_serial`` (default true) replaces
the serial number, in model 1's ``SN`` and anywhere else it appears, with
``<serial>``. The gateway's address and name are never included.

post.description:
On-demand read of a single SunSpec model from the device.

Connects to the controller, calls model.read() to fetch live register
values, then returns the point name→value map.  Also injects the values
into the sample bus so the Explorer sees them immediately.
Re-read a gateway's SunSpec model chain into its catalog.

get.description:
The latest points of the gateway named by ``?gateway=`` (ID or serial),
with its command state. No gateway named: 400 (#296 item 43).

Reads that gateway's own sample bus, never the global one: the global bus
carries every gateway's samples, and partial samples from one would blank
out another's fields.
One point of the gateway named by ``?gateway=``; 400 if none is named.

Return power time-series for the dashboard chart.

Supports two modes:
- **Relative range**: ``?range=30m`` (default) — last N from now.
- **Absolute date range**: ``?start=<epoch>&end=<epoch>`` — historical query.

Optional ``?bucket=5m`` downsamples to the given interval.
Valid buckets: 1m, 5m, 10m, 15m, 30m, 1h.
Return DB storage statistics (row counts, sizes, time ranges).

post.description: Manually trigger metrics archival (downsample old raw data).

get.description:
Return alarm events in a time window.

Provide either ``start``+``end`` (Unix timestamps) or ``range``
(e.g. ``30m``, ``1h``, ``24h``).  Events are sparse — only rows
written on register state changes are returned.

Return durationed alarm + PV-Clipping events in a time window.

Unlike ``/alarm-events`` (raw SET/CLR transitions), this pairs each
transition into a single row with a start time, end time, and
duration, and merges in PV-Clipping/Grid-Forming intervals derived
from ``metrics.grid_mode``. Same ``start``+``end`` / ``range`` params
as ``/alarm-events``.
Read metrics retention + raw-resolution config.

put.description:
Update metrics retention and/or the raw full-resolution window.

raw_age_days is how long full-resolution samples are kept before being
downsampled to 5-min buckets; it must be >= 1 and <= retention_days
(keeping raw longer than total retention is meaningless).

get.description: Return operational statistics (uptime, polls, errors, data quality).

Persisted log history, filterable by time span (start_ts/end_ts) + level/
gateway/source/search. Returned oldest-first (the UI reverses for display).
Falls back to the in-memory buffer on a fresh DB (default, no-range view).

post.description:
Execute a SunSpec Modbus sequence against one or all gateways.

It writes real registers (WSetEna/WSetPct included, i.e. a battery
dispatch), so it needs the ``control`` capability, and every run is
recorded in the control log with who ran it and what it wrote.

get.description: List saved sequence files.
Get a saved sequence file's content.

put.description: Save or update a sequence file.

post.description: Rename a sequence file.

get.description: The latest version's sample sequences on GitHub, marked new, changed or same.

post.description: Fetch (or take pasted) sequence text and check it. Saves and runs nothing.
Save a previewed sequence. Asks (``exists``) before replacing one.

get.description: Return all PICS compliance statuses.

put.description: Upsert a PICS compliance status for a model point.

get.description:
Battery power limits a force command may use: trusted ratings only (#133).
For the gateway named by ``?gateway=``; 400 if none is named.

post.description: Create a new database backup.

get.description: List available backups, newest first.

post.description:
Restore the database from a named backup.

Creates a pre-restore snapshot automatically.  The bridge should be
restarted after restore to reload state.

get.description: Download a backup archive as a ZIP file.

Export metrics as CSV or JSON for the given time range.

Unlike the chart endpoint, this returns every stored row (no
downsampling) so exports are lossless.

post.description:
Import metrics from a CSV file.

Expects columns: timestamp, battery_w, grid_w, solar_w, home_w, soc.
Timestamp can be ISO-8601 or Unix epoch float.

get.description:
The System view payload: every set-up gateway, default first, with both
layouts. Disabled and unconfigured gateways are left out; a stopped one is
drawn offline.

schema.title: Response Get System Api System Get

get.description:
The stored config, plus where each broker field in use comes from (#103).

``sources`` maps host/port/username/password to ``environment`` /
``settings`` / ``supervisor`` / ``default``; ``env_vars`` names the variable
for each field the environment sets, so the form can say why it's locked.
The namespace in use, the choices, and whether a change needs confirming.

post.description:
Change this bridge's MQTT namespace (#87). Admin-only (router gate).

Before anything is published it simply switches. After, ``confirm`` is
required: the old namespace's retained discovery configs that THIS bridge
wrote are removed (another producer's are left), then everything is
republished under the new one. The answer carries the counts.

Test TCP connectivity.  Accepts optional {host, port} in the body
to test *before* saving; falls back to the stored config.

get.description: List all publishing groups with member counts.

post.description: Create a new custom publishing group.

get.description:
Return the full entity catalog — all available entity definitions.

Used by the Settings UI to populate group member pickers.  Each entry
includes slug, name, ha_type, state_group, and whether it's a control
entity.
Return slugs of entities disabled by group settings.
Get a single group with its member list.

patch.description: Update name, description, or enabled state of a group.

delete.description: Delete a custom group. Default groups cannot be deleted.

get.description: List entity slugs in a group.

put.description: Replace all members of a group.

post.description: Add an entity to a group.

delete.description: Remove an entity from a group.

get.description: List the catalog points promoted into a group.

post.description: Promote a catalog point ("model.point") into a group.

delete.description: Remove a promoted point from a group (ref as ?ref=model.point).

get.description: Return site configuration.
Return aggregated site-level status from all gateways.

Detected timezone, whether a user ever confirmed it, and the local time
right now — so the prompt can show what the bridge believes rather than
asking the user to take it on trust.

post.description:
Record the user's decision, optionally correcting the timezone.

Correcting it here only changes what the bridge EXPECTS. The clock itself
comes from the container, so a correction must also be applied there (TZ in
docker-compose, or the Supervisor's setting) — otherwise the next start
reports a mismatch, which is the honest outcome rather than a silent
disagreement.

Close the current billing period and begin a new plan.

Totals reset at this boundary deliberately: a period must never span two
price sets, or its cost is an average of tariffs that were never both in
force. Closed periods keep their own snapshot of retailer/network/version,
so history reads as what it was.

get.description:
Export a service's tariff as a portable profile.

Identifying fields are stripped: sharing a plan should not share a meter
number, an account, or a network approval that belongs to one connection.

post.description:
Validate a tariff profile, and optionally apply it.

``dry_run=true`` (the default) reports what would happen without touching
anything — importing a tariff overwrites rates that price real money, so it
should never be a single unconfirmed click.

With ``service_id`` the profile is applied to that service, leaving its
identity and network grant intact. Without one, a new service is created.

Check a season/wave plan before it is saved.

Server-side because the resolver is the authority on what it will actually
price — a UI that validated separately would drift from it. Returns
``{ok, problems: [...]}`` where problems are plain sentences.

get.description:
How many closed billing periods this service produced — the UI uses it
to offer 'retire' instead of 'delete'.
List all electricity utility services.

post.description: Create a new utility service.

patch.description:
Update a utility service. exclude_unset so booleans/windows can be set to
false/null explicitly (e.g. clearing a tariff window).

delete.description:
Delete a utility service — refused once it has produced billing history.

Deleting would strand closed periods against a service that no longer
exists, which is exactly the continuity the history view is for. Retiring
(``enabled: false``) stops it pricing anything while keeping its rows.

get.description: List all gateways with live status from the registry.

post.description: Add a new gateway.

get.description: Get a single gateway with live status.

delete.description:
Remove a gateway. The row with ID 'default' can't be removed yet (D1);
if the designated default goes, the next gateway becomes the default.

post.description:
Designate the default gateway (#296 item 43): listed first, and the
page opens on it. A designation only; no gateway's identity changes.
Start polling a gateway.

Stop polling a gateway and remember the stop across restarts.

Sets ``autostart=0`` so the gateway is not re-started on the next app
boot.  ``enabled`` stays 1 — this is a user pause, not an admin disable,
so the gateway remains configured and can be started again.  This is what
keeps a stopped (esp. mock) gateway from self-restarting on reboot.

Tear down and recreate a gateway's Modbus connection.

Unlike /diagnose (read-only), this is the actual fix for a wedged
session: it discards the current GatewayInstance (closing whatever
socket state it had, good or bad) and reconnects from scratch, without
needing a full bridge process restart. ``registry.start_gateway``
already stops any existing instance for this ID before starting a new
one, so this is mechanically identical to /start — this endpoint exists
for a clear, explicit "restart" action in the UI/CLI regardless of
whether the gateway looked like it was already running.

get.description:
What a stop or restart would interrupt: each running gateway's dispatch.

A restart releases an active battery command, and a schedule whose window
is open fires again afterwards (docs/restarts-and-shutdown.md).

post.description:
Restart the whole bridge (Docker only): a graceful shutdown, then the
container's restart policy starts it again.

Force an immediate TCP health probe, instead of waiting for the
periodic HealthChecker (default: every 60s) to get to this gateway.

Updates the same ``status.health`` field the topbar dot reads, so the
UI reflects the result on its next refresh.

get.description:
Auto-detect the gateway's wired phase(s) from its 701 registers.

Reads the gateway's latest cached points (no extra Modbus traffic) and
infers connected/utilised phases. Also reports whether the result matches
the gateway's currently declared ``phase``.

post.description: Test TCP connectivity to a gateway's host:port.

Root-cause a Modbus connectivity problem for a gateway.

Runs TCP reachability probes (Modbus port + Local API port), a live
Modbus protocol-level read reusing the poller's existing session (never
opens a second concurrent Modbus session — see docs/vendor-issues.md on
concurrent-access corruption), and cross-checks the result against the
poller's own reported state to catch cases where the poller thinks it's
fine but isn't.

get.description: Get current points for a specific gateway.

post.description: Dispatch a control command to a specific gateway.

get.description:
Battery power limits a force command may use: trusted ratings only (#133).

``max_charge_w`` / ``max_discharge_w`` are None until the rating is
calibrated or Model 702 is confirmed by an observed peak; no 5000 W default.

The evidence behind this gateway's battery power rating, per direction (#133).

``trusted`` says whether force commands are allowed; ``reason`` says why
not and how to fix it. ``calibration`` is the window being recorded, if any.

post.description:
Record the battery's full-rate power while the owner runs a dispatch in the app.

Start, then in the FranklinWH app run a TOU battery dispatch (force charge
from grid, or force discharge to grid) with import and export unlimited, at
mid SoC. Finish after at least a minute: the peak becomes the calibrated
rating for that direction. The bridge sends nothing to the aGate here.

get.description:
Every battery command sent to this gateway and how it ended, newest first.

States: sent / failed / verified / not_effective / reasserted / released /
release_unverified / superseded (design PR #57 §5.1). ``requester`` says
who asked: ``schedule:<entry id>`` or ``manual``.

Hourly link health for one gateway: requests by kind and code path
(outcomes, latency), connections, reconnects, rescans, overlap, sockets.
Read-only measurement; the baseline the connection work is judged by.

Whether the wizard should open. Any signed-in user may ask; only admins
are shown the wizard (the UI checks the role).

post.description: Record a choice — typically ``skipped``, or ``pending`` to run it again.

get.description:
Subnets to search, each with where it came from (see environment.py).

Also the networks of aGates already set up here: an aGate reached over
Tailscale or a VPN lives on a network the bridge's host isn't on, so the
host's own interfaces never suggest it — but a second aGate is usually on
the same network as the first.

post.description: Search subnets for aGates in the background; poll ``GET /scan/{id}``.
Identify one address (the wizard's *Enter address → Test*).

Set up a real gateway at this address and start it.

The first one fills the primary gateway (internally still id ``default``,
which owns the unprefixed MQTT topics existing HA setups rely on); any
further ones are added alongside.

Create a demo (mock) gateway.

Always a separate gateway — never the primary: the primary owns the
unprefixed MQTT topics, and synthetic data there would land in the same HA
entities (and long-term statistics) a real aGate uses later.

Not published to Home Assistant until the user says so (#96): as an add-on
a demo used to put a "Demo aGate" device into the user's real HA unasked.

Record whether this install is used with Home Assistant (#94).

Not asked as an add-on, which always runs inside Home Assistant.

The wizard's "Publish <gateway>'s entities to Home Assistant?" (#96).

The same switch as ``PATCH /api/gateways/{id}`` ``publish_to_ha``, and
applied the same way — live: off removes the entities from HA, on
publishes them. Returns the checklist, which reflects the answer.

get.description:
Step 6: is everything between the bridge and Home Assistant working?

Each item is ``ok`` / ``fail`` / ``unknown`` (couldn't tell — shown as a
manual step) / ``skipped`` (not using Home Assistant), with a ``detail``.

Logins on this bridge, and which still have a password anyone would
try first ("admin", the username...). The shipped compose seeds
admin/admin, so a new install starts there.

Under HA ingress the bridge's own logins aren't used: ``applies`` is false.

All feature modules with resolved enabled state + ``can_access`` for the
current user's role. Drives the UI nav/tab gating and the admin Modules
panel.

patch.description: Enable/disable a module (admin). Core modules can't be disabled.

get.description:
Directional energy flows for a day (default today) or an explicit span.

``day`` is the common case and what the dashboards use. ``start``/``end``
epoch seconds cover week/month/year views without a second endpoint.

Per-hour battery charge/discharge for a local day (default today).

Feeds the Solar Forecast card's charging/discharging band. Integrated from
the sampled ``battery_w`` series (sign-split, so a mixed hour reports both
directions) — an estimate from sampled power, not a meter reading.
Hours after now carry ``state: null``.

Lifetime and period kWh, straight from the aGate's own counters.

Measured, not reconstructed — these are the figures to trust when they
disagree with the Sankey's arcs.

Projected out of the same sensor snapshot the Automation Builder and the
schedule engine read, rather than re-deriving the counters here. A second
derivation is a second thing to drift: the whole point of these being the
trustworthy numbers is that there is exactly one of them.
Current recording settings, plus the catalogue a client can offer.

put.description:
Update recording settings.

Takes effect on the next poll tick — the loop re-reads this each pass rather
than caching it, so there is nothing to restart. Shrinking retention does
not delete anything here; the purge pass applies it on its own schedule.

get.description:
Historical series for a comma-separated ``points`` list.

``bucket_s`` is chosen automatically from the span unless given. The
response echoes the resolved span and bucket so a caller can label the
axis with what it actually got rather than what it asked for.

What point history costs now, and what a candidate config would cost.

The projection query params let Settings show the consequence of a change
while the user is still deciding, without saving it first.

Weather + PV production forecast. Needs latitude/longitude set; otherwise
``{configured: false, reason}``. Cached 15 min; ``force`` refetches.
Location + PV array settings for the Settings form.

put.description: Update the location / PV array (only the fields sent).

post.description:
Use a configured Home Assistant's home location (its ``get_config``
latitude/longitude) as the forecast location, and save it.

get.description:
Live wholesale price: the AEMO NEM spot for ``region`` (default: the
configured one) and the configured HA price entities, plus the ACTIVE
buy/sell (HA wins per side over NEM). No region and nothing configured ->
``spot: null``, and nothing is fetched.
NEM region + HA price entities, for the Settings form.

put.description: Update the NEM region / HA price entities (only the fields sent).

get.description:
The live price a dynamic plan is (or would be) priced at.

With no ``source``: the ACTIVE plan's provider and the live price billing
is using now (``live`` is null for a static plan). With ``source`` (``nem``
+ ``region``, or ``ha`` + ``buy_entity`` [+ ``feedin_entity``]): a preview
for the tariff editor, before anything is saved. Invalid input -> 422.

The notice text, and whether this user has already accepted this version.

Returns the text as well as the flag so the UI never keeps its own copy of
the wording — one source, and a version bump can't leave a stale paragraph
rendered next to a fresh version number.

post.description: Record acceptance. Declining is answered honestly rather than stored.

get.description:
The acknowledgement trail. Admin-only — it is a record of who agreed to
what, which is nobody else's business.
Alerts newest first, with where each was delivered. Any signed-in role.

parameters.name: open

schema.description: only alerts that still need someone
schema.title: Open

parameters.description: only alerts that still need someone

parameters.name: since

schema.description: epoch seconds; last activity at or after
schema.title: Since

parameters.description: epoch seconds; last activity at or after

schema.title: Response Get Alerts Api Alerts Get

post.description: Acknowledge for everyone (admin). Recorded as ``user:<name>``.

get.description: Whether critical alerts also go to Home Assistant (on by default).

put.description: Switch HA notifications on or off (admin). Off never hides the bridge's modal.

get.description:
Every SunSpec write: time, register, raw values, the aGate's reply, who asked.

No serial or IP is in these rows, so nothing needs masking.

The app log for the Logs tab's filter, as a file; serials and IPs masked (#320).

Same filters as ``GET /api/logs``. Oldest first; past ``limit`` the newest are kept.

Redacted summary of this install, as JSON and as Markdown.

No serials, IPs, host names, ports, MAC addresses, location, usernames,
emails, HA URLs or tokens, passwords, MQTT credentials or client id, or
device names. Log messages are scrubbed by pattern — review before posting.

post.description: Run the franklinwh-modbus reader against a gateway. Admin, read-only.

get.description: List all schedule entries with active-now / next-fire previews.

post.description: Create a schedule entry.

get.description:
Export schedules as a portable JSON bundle. ``ids`` = comma-separated
entry ids (default: all).

post.description:
Validate (and optionally create) an imported bundle. ``dry_run=true``
(default) returns a per-entry validation report without creating anything;
``dry_run=false`` creates the valid entries DISABLED (for review), with any
unknown gateway target falling back to Default.

get.description:
Recent schedule dispatch/audit events (newest first).

Optional filters: ``schedule_id`` (one entry's runs) and ``status`` (the
audit result: fired/gated/missed/executed/exit_condition_met/…) — this backs
the FWHAI audit + history views.

post.description:
Fire a schedule entry's action now (respects entry_conditions unless
``?force=true``). The dispatch auto-releases after the entry's duration.

Gracefully stop a schedule's CURRENT run: release the live dispatch it
owns and skip re-firing until the next scheduled window. The entry stays
enabled (disable it to stop permanently).

get.description:
Return the day's windows per entry for the visual timeline.

``day`` is an optional weekday (0=Mon..6=Sun) to preview; defaults to today.
Each segment is minutes-from-midnight so the UI can lay out a 24h bar.
Get one schedule entry.

patch.description:
Update a schedule entry.

Uses ``exclude_unset`` so we apply exactly the fields the client sent —
including explicit nulls. A previous ``if v is not None`` filter silently
dropped nulls, which made it impossible to CLEAR a field: deleting all
exit_conditions (client sends ``exit_conditions: null``) never persisted.
``update_schedule`` stores None as SQL NULL for the nullable JSON columns.

get.description: The command vocabulary a schedule entry can dispatch (for the UI form).

Sensor namespace + current values for the condition-builder dropdowns.

Includes the static Bridge sensors plus any HA entities (``ha:<inst>:<entity>``)
so the Automation Builder can condition on Home Assistant state.

User-defined automation constants (min/max/demand SoC) + their [min,max]
bounds for the settings form. Surfaced as ``const.*`` sensors too.

put.description: Update automation constants (only sent fields; each clamped to [0,100]).

post.description:
Evaluate a condition tree against the gateway's live snapshot.

Returns ``{result: bool, per_condition: [{sensor, op, value, live_value,
result}]}`` — the Test Verification response.

get.description:
Debug monitor: one line per enabled entry per scheduler tick.

Kept in memory only (the last ``MONITOR_MAX`` lines, lost on restart).
``since`` is the last ``seq`` the caller has, so a poll gets only new lines.
Configured HA instances (tokens redacted) + live connection status.

post.description:
Probe a base_url/token WITHOUT saving — powers the config form's Test button.

On an edit the token field is blank; if ``ha_id`` is given we fall back to
that instance's stored token so Test reflects the real (saved) credentials
instead of failing 401 with no auth.

Returns ``{connected, entity_count, last_error}``.

get.description:
Available ``notify.*`` services across all HA instances.

Notify targets are services, not entities, so they never appear in the
entity browser — the action picker needs them from here.

Browse ALL HA entities across instances (with an ``exposed`` flag),
filtered + paginated — backs the HA Entities tab.

Filters: ``instance`` (id), ``domain``, ``search`` (substring of entity_id or
friendly name), ``exposed`` (true/false). Returns
``{total, page, page_size, exposed_count, entities:[...]}``.

``search`` accepts **comma-separated terms matched as OR** — real
installations name the same concept a dozen ways ("pv", "solar",
"enphase", "envoy"), so a single substring misses most of a topic. A
plain term without commas behaves exactly as before.
Distinct entity domains across all instances (for the filter dropdown).

post.description: Add/remove an entity from an instance's allowlist (persists + applies live).

get.description:
Copy-paste HA dashboard card YAML for this bridge's entities (#86).

Entity ids come only from the chosen HA instance's device + entity
registries — never predicted. Returns ``{yaml, entity_count, devices,
instance, layout}``; 409/503 with a ``detail`` (and no YAML) when the
registry can't be read or holds none of our entities.

This bridge's published entities and what HA calls them: entity id,
diagnostic or not, the bridge dashboard's label, and whether the id is the
bridge's own form. Read from HA's registries, like the dashboard card.
Setup config + live period values + linked automations for the tab.

Closed billing periods (reporting/history), most-recent first.

Each period carries the plan(s) in force during it, so a period that
straddles a retailer switch can be flagged rather than silently reported
under one retailer's name.
Plan history for a service, oldest first.

post.description:
Record a plan change, closing the plan that was in force at that date.

Inserting *between* two existing plans is supported — that is what recording
history you did not capture at the time means.

patch.description:
Correct a plan's start date.

Needed because a backfilled plan starts at the placeholder migration 45 had
nothing better to use, leaving no earlier instant at which to insert a
predecessor. The real start has to be settable *first*, then the earlier
retailer can be recorded before it.

get.description: Closed billing periods as a CSV download (chronological).

Serve the main SPA shell. Unauthenticated → /login; non-admin → /user;
an api account gets the "REST API only" page.

The simplified, mobile-first end-user dashboard. Any signed-in role may
view it (admins can preview it here); unauthenticated → /login.
The login form. Already-authenticated users go to their role's home.

post.description:
Dispatch a control command (same path as MQTT commands) to the
gateway named by ``gateway_id`` in the body; 400 if none is named.
``POST /api/gateways/{gw_id}/command`` does the same with the gateway in
the path.
Log an outage the browser saw (it couldn't reach the bridge).

AckRequest.title: AckRequest
AckRequest.description:
``agreed`` false is a real answer, not a no-op.

The modal's Continue button is enabled either way: refusing to let someone
close a dialog is not consent, it is a hostage situation. Declining simply
isn't recorded, so the notice comes back next time — which is the behaviour
asked for, and is honest about what did and didn't happen.

AlertSettingsUpdate.description: Each field is optional: only those given change.

covered_s.description: Seconds of the hour that had samples

state.title: State
state.description: Dominant direction; null = no samples (future hour or outage)

BatteryHour.title: BatteryHour
BatteryHour.description: One hour of battery activity, integrated from sampled ``battery_w``.

idle_kwh.title: Idle Kwh
idle_kwh.description: Below this per hour an hour counts as idle

ConfigPatch.title: ConfigPatch
ConfigPatch.description:
Partial update. Absent fields keep their current value.

Bounds are enforced in :func:`point_history.get_config` as well — these are
here so a bad request is a 422 with a field name rather than a silent clamp.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: the ACTIVE plan's pricing kind: static|dynamic

dynamic.title: Dynamic
dynamic.description: the provider shown (the preview's, else the active plan's)

note.title: Note
note.default: Energy is priced at the live rate. Demand, export-bonus, export-charge and standing charges still apply on top. With no live price for a slice, that energy is recorded as unpriced.

HaActionItem.title: HaActionItem
HaActionItem.description:
One one-shot HA action. ``when`` selects the edge it runs on: ``fire``
(activation) or ``exit`` (when the window/activation ends).

Two kinds:
- ``entity`` (default) — a service call on an entity (turn_on, select_option…).
- ``notify`` — a one-way message via an HA ``notify.*`` service. It has no
  entity: ``service`` is the notify target name and title/message carry the
  content, so entity_id is not required for it.

LinkStatsRow.title: LinkStatsRow
LinkStatsRow.description:
One ``link_stats`` row. Request rows fill the request columns; the
``kind = 'link'`` row fills the connection-level ones. See
``franklinwh_bridge.gateway.link_stats`` for what each column means.

valid_from.title: Valid From
valid_from.description: epoch seconds; may be in the past

PlanChange.title: PlanChange
PlanChange.description:
A retailer/plan switch, recorded at the date it actually happened.

``valid_from`` is almost always in the past: a switch is discovered after
the fact, and stamping it "now" is what made the owner's own Amber → AGL
change on 09 Sep unrepresentable.

PlanStartCorrection.title: PlanStartCorrection
PlanStartCorrection.description: Move a plan's start date without creating a new plan.

PlanSwitch.title: PlanSwitch
PlanSwitch.description:
Start a new plan on a service. Both fields optional — switching plan with
the same retailer (a re-contract) is as common as changing supplier.

pv_azimuth.title: Pv Azimuth
pv_azimuth.description: Open-Meteo convention: 0 = south, -90 = east, 90 = west, ±180 = north.

SolarSettingsBody.title: SolarSettingsBody
SolarSettingsBody.description:

azimuth_help.title: Azimuth Help

SpotSettingsBody.title: SpotSettingsBody
